memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "It is not up in heaven, so that you have to ask, 'Who will ascend into heaven to get it and proclaim it to us so we may obey it?' Nor is it beyond the sea, so that you have to ask, 'Who will cross the sea to get it and proclaim it to us so we may obey it?' No, the word is very near you; it is in your mouth and in your heart so you may obey it." — Deut 30:12-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God's word, Moses says, is not far off and inaccessible — not up in heaven or across a distant sea, requiring some heroic quest to reach it. No, "the word is very near you; it is in your mouth and in your heart." God had made His truth accessible and clear. His people did not need to climb to heaven or cross an ocean to find it. It was right there with them.

What a comfort this is. We sometimes imagine that knowing God requires some extraordinary journey, some hidden knowledge available only to spiritual elites. But God has drawn near. His word is accessible to ordinary people — the child, the labourer, the elderly believer — not locked away for scholars alone. He has made Himself known.

The New Testament takes this passage and reveals its deepest meaning. Paul quotes these very verses in Romans 10 and applies them to the gospel. We do not need to ascend to heaven to bring Christ down or descend to the depths to raise Him up — because Christ has already come, already died, already risen. The "word that is near" is now "the message concerning faith": if you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved (Rom 10:8-9).

Do you see the wonder? Salvation is not a distant, unreachable thing. In Christ, it is as near as your own mouth and heart. You do not have to earn your way up to God — He has come near to you. Simply believe and receive Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I ever think knowing God requires some extraordinary journey?
2. How does it change things to know God's word — and salvation — is near?
3. Have I received the "word of faith" by trusting in the risen Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You have come near and made Yourself known. I do not have to climb to heaven to reach You, for in Christ You reached down to me. I confess Jesus as Lord and believe in my heart. Amen.
